host.exposure: edge bound to 127.0.0.1:28080/28443 (TCP) and 127.0.0.1:28443 (UDP); no public port opened

versions.application: the RagX API image and the client and admin web images, pinned by digest in a loopback registry

protocols.method: benches/protocols.sh: 2000 requests per round, 16 parallel, one curl binary for both protocols, inside the apps network to edge:8443, API /health behind HAProxy, edge CPU from the container cgroup; wall time includes the client container start
protocols.reading: On a loss-free sub-millisecond path HTTP/3 brings no edge advantage: about 7% lower throughput, equal CPU. Its value is on lossy, high-RTT client paths, which this lab does not model.
proof: curl --http3-only through the published UDP port 127.0.0.1:28443 answered HTTP/3 200
HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 over TCP answered 200 with X-Release, Alt-Svc h3=":28443", HSTS, X-Request-ID, nosniff and no Server header
plain HTTP answered 308 to HTTPS; an unknown Host answered 404

guards: redeploying inside the retention window refused: slot keeps the previous release for rollback
a live WebSocket on the retiring slot made the deploy wait 30 s and refuse; after the session closed the deploy succeeded
a concurrent deploy refused on the lock (exit 1) while the first completed
a stale lock with a dead owner blocked deploys until recover --force, which resumed idempotently
edge drift refused before any slot retirement until edge apply
edge apply hot-reloaded HAProxy (container kept, new worker) and kept the previous configuration for rollback
an unpinned API_IMAGE failed validation with exit 1

refusals: a dump whose checksum does not match

control_plane.portainer: installed on loopback with a private CA whose key is deleted after issuance, verified TLS, an API key minted into a mode-600 secret, the pull registry registered through the API
control_plane.export: the desired Compose artifact keeps ${API_REPLICAS}, ${DEPLOY_SLOT} and ${RELEASE_ROOT}, carries no host path or secret, and validates with docker compose under Portainer-style variables

unverified: Docker Hub private push and pull: no Docker Hub credentials were supplied; the driver differs from GHCR only in host and Portainer type, both covered by offline tests
public UDP 443 through a cloud firewall and Let's Encrypt issuance: they need a public domain and an open cloud firewall; the HTTP-01 route and the certbot arguments are verified
the live Cloudflare API: no account token; the create, update, IPv6 and proxied request flows are pinned by offline tests

private_git_and_registry.where: GitHub Actions run 39214929789 in the private repository comstrx/infra-lab-gitops, Ubuntu 24.04 runner with Docker 28.0.4 and Compose 2.38.2; the job-scoped GITHUB_TOKEN reached the tool only through REGISTRY_TOKEN and GITOPS_TOKEN in the environment
private_git_and_registry.registry: registry login and registry push sent the RagX API image to private ghcr.io/comstrx/lab-api, every local copy was removed, and the deploy pulled it back by digest with the stored credentials; portainer registry registered ghcr.io with authentication
private_git_and_registry.gitops: reconcile cloned the private branch and the protected release tag, verified the desired files and Compose checksum, and Portainer created authenticated Git stacks from the private repository whose GitConfig.ConfigHash equaled the verified commit

lifecycle.scenario: branch desired state tampered after tagging
lifecycle.result: refused: Tagged desired state differs from the branch
switched back, X-Release of the first release

private_git_and_registry.audit: no token in release files, edge, data, desired state or Git history; registry config, API key and api.env at mode 600

macos: GitHub Actions macos-latest: the release bundle ran plan, installed the launchd timer (state active, run interval 3600 s), and removed it

wan.where: GitHub Actions run 39219122915, Ubuntu 24.04 runner, client container on the apps network with tc netem on its egress, 1000 requests per round, 16 parallel, curl 8.23.0 (ngtcp2 1.22.1, nghttp3 1.15.0, GnuTLS 3.8.13)
wan.reading: Without loss the protocols tie. Under loss HTTP/3 keeps its throughput and median while HTTP/2 suffers TCP head-of-line blocking: about 1.3x throughput at 1% loss and 1.7x at 3%, at roughly 15-25% more edge CPU.

backup_s3: GitHub Actions run 39218228393: SeaweedFS S3 gateway with enforced credentials (a wrong secret is refused); backup with BACKUP_DRIVER=s3 uploaded the dump and its checksum through the aws CLI, and the downloaded copy matched the local backup
acme_route: GitHub Actions run 39218228393: a server with network alias acme on the apps network served /.well-known/acme-challenge/ over plain HTTP through the edge while every other path answered 308 to HTTPS

production_rehearsal.where: the 4 vCPU rootless-Docker server, DEPLOY_ENV=production, release bundle staged over SSH, ports 28080/28443 because the cloud firewall and missing sudo block 80/443, public names under 8-228-211-196.sslip.io with a rehearsal CA
production_rehearsal.images: the RagX API and the client and admin web specs built on the server from the current source with image build, pinned by digest in a loopback registry
checks: first deploy ran the expand migration, passed readiness and switched; Docker 29.9.1 and Compose 5.6.0 matched Bash.toml
through the edge: register 201 over HTTP/2, login issued a token, /v1/auth/me 200 with it and 401 without it
the client site answered 307 (locale redirect) and the admin site 200; HTTP/3 through the published UDP port answered the API 200, the client 307 and the admin 200
the worker consumed the welcome mail queued by registration through RabbitMQ; worker and scheduler logs carried no error
release r2 to r3 under load: 60000 of 60000 requests answered 200
rollback r3 to r2 under load: 40000 of 40000 requests answered 200
fixed: slot retirement checked HAProxy sessions even when no edge existed, which blocked every redeploy after a first deploy that failed before the edge started
the public probe needed hairpin NAT in production; without EXTERNAL_HEALTH_URL it now resolves the API host to the local bind address
export needed every application secret; it now renders only the Compose files
CI baked api.example.invalid into the web images; the API host and HTTPS port now come from repository variables
production_rehearsal.left_for_the_real_host: ports 80 and 443 with Let's Encrypt, public UDP 443 and browser access from the internet
